issue.title: Status of testing Providers that were prepared on October 14, 2026
issue.body:
I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

This is an ad-hoc wave that re-cuts the four providers excluded from the 2026-10-06 wave (#74459) now that the regressions found there are fixed - amazon, dbt.cloud and google at rc2, and common.ai as its first stable release, 1.0.0rc1 (it was 0.11.0rc1 in the previous wave). common.compat 1.22.0rc1 is included because the new amazon EMR Serverless session operator needs it.

Items already verified in #74459 are pre-ticked - no need to test them again. Please focus on the unticked ones, especially the fixes for the regressions that caused the exclusions (#74529, #74489, #74505, #74525, #74537) together with the changes they fix.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:

comments.body: Hi @potiuk, I'd like to independently verify #74505 against Google provider 22.7.0rc2, focusing on compatibility with older Kubernetes providers. I'll report the installed versions, import results, and exception behavior.

Verified #74192 with `apache-airflow-providers-google==22.7.0rc2` from PyPI (Airflow 3.3.2, Python 3.12):

- the three Dataproc triggers (`DataprocSubmitTrigger`, `DataprocSubmitJobDirectTrigger`, `DataprocClusterTrigger`) re-raise `CancelledError` after their cleanup — checked the code in the installed package, the bare `raise` is there in all three.
- ran the updated trigger tests from main against the installed RC: 52 passed, 5 skipped (the skips are the `on_kill()` tests that defer to the Airflow 3.3+ cancellation path, as expected).

Tested following providers and all work as expected.

- amazon 9.38.0rc2
  - #74529: A login started from Airflow works again over HTTPS.
- dbt.cloud 4.11.0rc2
  - #74489: A deferrable `DbtCloudRunJobOperator` with tenacity objects in `hook_params["retry_args"]` defers and succeeds. The worker task log now shows one warning for the dropped `retry_args`, and the trigger retries with `retry_limit` and `retry_delay`.
- common.ai 1.0.0rc1
  - #74537: Output functions, `TypeAliasType` and `NewType` now push a dict, so a downstream `xcom_pull` no longer raises `ImportError`.`str` and `[str, int]` answers stay strings. `dict` and `list[str]` outputs now come back as a dict and a list instead of a Python repr string.
  - #74525: A deep-copied `SandboxToolset` can work again.

Verified the basic live backend flows for #71672 (Islo) and #71725 (Boat) with `apache-airflow-providers-common-ai[boat,islo]==1.0.0rc1` installed from PyPI, Airflow 3.3.2, Python 3.12.12 (`islo==0.3.20`, `boat-sdk==1.9.9`).

Both passed sandbox creation, command execution with preserved newlines, file write/read round-trip, directory listing, nonzero exit-code handling, and sandbox destruction. Boat used one sandbox for all checks with `SandboxSpec(block_network=False)`; Islo used the default `SandboxSpec()`.

This was a direct backend smoke test, not an AgentOperator/Dag or full system-test run; timeout and network enforcement were not exercised. #73961 (OpenShell) and #74504 (OpenSandbox dns+nft enforcement) remain unverified by this run. #71676 is already checked in the issue.

Follow-up for #73961 (OpenShell) and #74504 (OpenSandbox dns+nft enforcement): ran the upstream `test_openshell.py` and `test_opensandbox.py` unit suites from main against the installed PyPI `apache-airflow-providers-common-ai==1.0.0rc1` package (Airflow 3.3.2, Python 3.12.12, macOS; `openshell==0.1.4`, `opensandbox==1.1.1`).

- OpenShell: 143 passed; 18 Linux-only guest-wrapper cases skipped because they require `/proc` and `setsid`.
- OpenSandbox: all 85 passed, including enforced-policy read-back, rejecting unenforced/address-layer policies with sandbox destruction, and owned-transport behavior with proxy environment variables.
- Total: 228 passed, 18 skipped, no failures (5.75 s).

These are unit results with mocked services, not live OpenShell/OpenSandbox service verification. Together with the live Islo/Boat smoke checks above, this reports the available verification for all five @zozo123 entries; #71676 was already checked. Leaving release checklist acceptance to the release manager.

Tested common.ai 1.0.0rc1 from the PyPI wheel on Airflow 3.3.2 (Python 3.12), with live runs against Claude Sonnet 5.5, TypeSafe Jev and Modal sandboxes. Also ran the Airflow 2.11.2 path, and Airflow 3.4.0b1 for the 3.4-only features.

Works as described in the PRs:

- #74385, #74704, #74314, #73873, #74720, #74313 (durable execution): a retry replays completed model steps and tool calls instead of running them again (a side-effecting tool ran once across two tries). A tool whose result couldn't be recorded is named and runs again. Answers the output validator rejected are asked again, not replayed. Usage with `audio_seconds` loads on every resume.
- #74396, #73706 (usage and spend across retries): attempt 2 hits `UsageLimitExceeded` early because attempt 1's requests count, and the failed attempt's `usage` XCom holds its own usage.
- #74308, #74707 (retry policies): with `include_traceback=True` the chained traceback reaches the classifier; `ClassifierRetryPolicy` on Jev picks retry or fail per category and escalates a below-bar answer to `LLMRetryPolicy`.
- #73994 (prompt caching): a repeated task reads from the cache, and `cache_prompt=False` turns it off.
- #73962, #73898, #73587, #73901, #74404 (framework adapters): the Anthropic tool runner, Strands and Google ADK examples run unmodified, with masked tool results and `common_ai.tool_calls` counted per framework. A Strands task resumes from its checkpoint on retry and re-runs only the failed tool.
- #73532 (managed-agent contract): exercised with a stub implementation of the hook contract, including failover and refusals. The Bedrock and Vertex hooks themselves were not exercised.
- #73586, #74686, #73904, #74450, #74351, #74272, #72202 (tool approval and HITL), under a real scheduler and API server: approve and reject both behave, multi-step approval works on 3.4.0b1 (and fails cleanly on 3.3 as documented), the approved typed answer reaches a downstream task, an unreadable review XCom fails after 10 reads, and review by map index and by loop pass touches only that slot.
- #73899, #73925, #70433, #73900, #74380, #74447, #74449, #73957, #74448, #73897, #73993, #73938, #73984, #74312, #72002, #74626 (toolsets): checked live with an agent where the model is involved. Secrets in tool output reach the model as `***` from toolsets, capabilities and retry messages alike. #74662 was checked offline (the batch submission itself was stubbed).
- #73418, #74302, #73990, #73559 (Modal): the `modal` connection authenticates with no ambient credentials, and an agent ran commands, exported a file to object storage, and attached to a sandbox another task provisioned. (The Modal provider was 0.1.0rc1 in this environment.)
- #74705, #73896, #74679 (lifecycle): production lifecycle, and no experimental warnings on the graduated features. The old usage in each 1.0.0 migration note fails as described and the new usage works; two notes overstate details (below).

Found, with fixes in open PRs for 1.0.1. None of them blocks this release:

- #74381: `AgentSkillsToolset` itself works, but a fresh `[skills]` install resolves pydantic-ai-skills 2.1.0, which removed `SkillsToolset`, so every run fails. 0.10.0 is affected the same way. #74899 caps it below 2.
- #74334: the Model tab never loads on 3.4.0b1, because it scopes on `operator_names` and core expects `operator_name`. Only affects 3.4, which is in beta. #74898.
- `durable=True` with duplicate toolset ids, or a tool that defers, fails with pydantic-ai errors instead of the documented ones. #74902, which also makes the changelog's "unique `id=`" note true.
- The changelog's `get_schema` note says to check `truncated` first, but a full result has no `truncated` key. #74904.
- Stale rows on the supported services page (#72939) and other docs fixes: #74904. Example Dags that never reach their feature against a real model: #74901. The pydantic-ai first-run banner in task logs when Airflow is started from a coding agent: #74900.
#74000 has been tested and is working as expected.

Verified dbt.cloud 4.11.0rc2 for #74199 on Airflow 3.4.0, Python 3.12.3, tenacity 9.1.4.

One script run unchanged against three provider versions, with `DbtCloudRunJobOperator(deferrable=True, hook_params={"retry_limit": 7, "retry_args": {"stop": stop_after_attempt(3)}})` and the hook mocked, so this covers the serialization boundary rather than a live dbt Cloud run. In all three the task defers and the job is recorded as started before it does.

- 4.10.0: the trigger receives no `hook_params`, so the hook in the trigger is built with none of them. Serializing the trigger arguments succeeds.
- 4.11.0rc1: the trigger receives `retry_args` and `retry_limit`, and putting the trigger arguments through `airflow.sdk.serde.serialize`, which is what `Trigger.encrypt_kwargs` uses to store them, raises `TypeError: Cannot serialize object of type <class 'tenacity.stop.stop_after_attempt'>`. The job is already started at that point, which is the orphaned run that kept dbt.cloud out of the previous wave.
- 4.11.0rc2: the trigger keeps `retry_limit`, logs a warning naming `retry_args` as dropped, and the trigger arguments serialize. `DbtCloudHook` builds from what survived.

Only the values that fail the JSON check are dropped. Given `retry_limit`, `retry_delay` and a tenacity `retry_args` together, rc2 keeps `retry_limit` and `retry_delay` and drops only `retry_args`. The operator half keeps all three, since the operator builds its own hook from the unfiltered mapping. The trigger docstring describes this.

`operators/dbt.py` and `triggers/dbt.py` in the rc2 wheel are byte identical by sha256 to the same files at current main `20ccfcd7457a`, and they are the only source files #74199 and #74489 changed between them.

Verified #69739 with apache-airflow-providers-dbt-cloud==4.11.0rc2 (Airflow 3.3.2, Python 3.12).

Ran the same script against 4.10.0 and 4.11.0rc2, calling `execute_complete` directly on `DbtCloudRunJobOperator(deferrable=True)` and `DbtCloudJobRunSensor(deferrable=True)` with the hook mocked:

- `event=None`: `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` on 4.10.0 -> `DbtCloudTriggerEventException` on rc2 (operator and sensor)
- unknown status (`"foo"`): marked success on 4.10.0 -> raises `DbtCloudTriggerEventException` on rc2 (operator and sensor)
- sensor `status="timeout"`: marked success on 4.10.0 -> `DbtCloudJobRunException` with the trigger's message on rc2
- sensor `error`/`cancelled`: empty `AirflowException` on 4.10.0 -> `DbtCloudJobRunException` with the trigger's message on rc2
- `status="success"` still succeeds, and the operator's `timeout`/`error`/`cancelled` handling is unchanged

Works as expected.

Validated the following changes included in the current provider release candidates:

- `apache-airflow-providers-google==22.7.0rc2` — #74505: verified compatibility with Kubernetes provider `10.21.0`: existing GKE operators remain usable, while `GKEPodExecOperator` raises the expected dependency-version error with the original import error preserved. Also verified with Kubernetes `10.24.0`; focused regression tests passed (`13 passed in 6.63s`).
- `apache-airflow-providers-google==22.7.0rc2` — #72577: `example_kubernetes_engine.py` passed against real GKE Autopilot (`1 passed in 1073.04s`), including command execution in an existing Pod, XCom output verification, and Pod/cluster cleanup. An independent cluster listing confirmed cleanup. The first attempt hit a Pod scheduling timeout; the unchanged system test passed on rerun without increasing timeouts.

Environment: Breeze, Airflow `3.3.2`, Python `3.11.16`; Google provider installed from the PyPI RC wheel, Kubernetes `10.21.0` for compatibility checks and `10.24.0` for regression/system tests.

Unable to verify #73099 at this time — I don't have the Airflow + provider rc environment available to run the test. Please uncheck the box for #73099; I'll revisit if I can set up the test environment later. Apologies for the delay.

The providers prepared on 2026-10-14 are released: amazon 9.38.0, common.compat 1.22.0, dbt.cloud 4.11.0 and google 22.7.0. common.ai 1.0.0 was excluded and will follow as 1.0.0rc2, with the pydantic-ai-skills cap from #74899, in a separate ad-hoc wave with an accelerated vote. Thanks to everyone who tested the release candidates!
